question.text: This modern-day Balkan country staged a decades-long revolt against Ottoman rule in the 15th century led by Skanderbeg. In the 20th century, it was ruled by the dictator Enver Hoxha (HOE-juh).
question.clue: Its King Zog was deposed by Mussolini, who attempted to invade Greece from this country, and it was formerly ruled by the communist dictator Enver Hoxha ("ho-sha").

swap.leadin: Its source is in the Black Forest region of Germany.
swap.text: Name this river that flows through Vienna long before it reaches the Black Sea.
swap.clue: Despite not being native to it, the Phanariotes served as administrators of a region on this river.

question.text: This former Yugoslav President was tried for war crimes at The Hague, but died in prison in of a heart attack in 2006 while still awaiting a verdict.
question.clue: He was overthrown in the 2000 Bulldozer Revolution.

swap.leadin: A country is not actually a country until the United Nations officially recognizes it. Identify these "wannabe" nations.
swap.text: With its capital at Pristina and a population of mostly Albanians, it declared independence from Serbia in 2008, but Russia blocked its recognition with a veto.
swap.clue: This country was the location of a battle where Ottoman Sultan Murad I was killed, while a war named for this modern day nation involved Operation Noble Anvil and was waged largely by the KLA.

question.leadin: The destroyed Vukovar Water Tower was preserved to commemorate massacres against this country's people.
question.text: Name this country which was led in its war of independence by Franjo Tudjman. Separatists in this country led the Log Revolution and bombarded the medieval Old Town of Dubrovnik.
question.clue: This country was merged with Slavonia in 1868, though Rijeka ] remained separate.

swap.leadin: In 1981, a leader of this country banned typewriters because he feared citizens were using them to write messages to foreign embassies detailing the conditions in his country.
swap.text: Name this country whose dictator Nicolae Ceausescu declared contraception illegal under Decree 770 in an attempt to increase this country's population.
swap.clue: A ruler of this country embraced a "mini-Cultural Revolution" as part of a return to socialist realism in the July Theses.

question.text: This group's leaders perpetrated the Bosnian genocide. The country that takes its name from this ethnic group has its capital at Belgrade.
question.clue: This people's mythology celebrates a man named Milos who walked into an enemy's tent under a white flag and then began stabbing him in the face.

swap.text: As a result of the last Russo-Turkish War, this country gained autonomy from Ottoman rule. Boris III was a tsar of this modern-day nation, whose capital city is Sofia.
swap.clue: This country pursued the Treaty of Craiova to recover territory lost in the Treaty of Neuilly, its "second national catastrophe," which saw it lose Southern Dobruja.

question.leadin: This people's leader Asparukh led them south to settle in Moesia and established their first empire at Pliska.
question.text: Name this nomadic people that also formed a state on the Volga River that was conquered by the Mongols. A later state of these people was ruled by the Asen dynasty.
question.clue: Many members of this ethnicity were killed by bashi-bazouk (BYE-jee-buh-ZOOK) soldiers during the April Uprising in namesake "horrors."

swap.text: Former capitals of this region include Campulung and Curtea de Arges. Distinct from the mountainous Transylvania, for 15 points, name this region that contains Bucharest, and that united with Moldavia to form Romania.
swap.clue: This region was the first one to be ruled by Michael the Brave.

question.leadin: This man declared that mothers of at least ten children were "heroine mothers."
question.text: Name this Communist leader executed along with his wife Elena on Christmas Day, 1989. He replaced Gheorghe Gheorghiu-Dej as General Secretary of his country's Communist Party in 1965.
question.clue: In an effort to increase his country's population, he outlawed almost all forms ofcontraception in Decree 770, and he employed a secret police known as the Securitate.

swap.leadin: This man used a fortress at Poenari Castle.
swap.text: Name this Prince of Wallachia still considered a folk hero in Romania. He is best known today for reportedly brutally executing his enemies, such as the Ottomans, by penetrating them with stakes.
swap.answerHtml: Vlad the Impaler [or Vlad Tepes; or Vlad III; or Vlad Dracula]
swap.clue: His younger brother Radu the Handsome spent most of his life as a hostage in Adrianople but returned to overthrow him in 1462, leading to his exile at the court of Matthias Corvinus until a later reconquest of Tirgoviste.

question.leadin: During the Log Revolution, people native to one of these two modern-day countries constructed blockades made of logs in the other, rejecting changes made after a 1990 election.
question.text: Name these two former members of Yugoslavia. Paramilitary units from one of them perpetrated the Vukovar Massacre in the other.
question.answerHtml: Serbia and Croatia [or Republic of Serbia and Republic of Croatia; accept Republika Hrvatska in place of “Croatia”; accept Republika Srbija in place of “Serbia”; do not accept answers mentioning “Republika Srpska,” because that’s different]

swap.leadin: Besides Germany, this country contributed the most troops to the fascist invasion of the USSR.
swap.text: Name this country, which lost Bessarabia and North Bukovina in the Molotov-Ribbentrop Pact and then regained those territories in Operation Barbarossa. This country's Conducator overthrew its king Carol II.
swap.clue: Though briefly restored by King Michael's Coup, this country's monarchy was abolished and replaced by the Iron Guard in 1940.

question.text: As the Red Army marched into Romania, this King launched a coup against Antonescu and joined the Allies. The Soviet post-war occupation forced his abdication and exile until the overthrow of Nicolae Ceausescu.

swap.leadin: The Treaty of San Stefano prompted Abdyl Frasheri to lead the League of Prizren in resistance against the partition of lands inhabited by this ethnic group.
swap.text: Name these people whose first prime minister Ismail Qemali waved the flag from the Assembly of Vlore ("VLAW-ruh") after declaring independence in 1912.
swap.clue: This ethnicity's Bushati and Muzaka families fought a series of 18th-century proxy conflicts named for sanjaks of Scutari and Berat.

question.text: Peter's monarchy was destroyed by this leader of the Partisans and Cominform in Yugoslavia, who served as its dictator all the way through to 1980.
question.clue: With the help of his secret police, the UDBA, this man ruled through the Informbiro schism as the leader of Yugoslavia from World War II until 1980.

swap.leadin: Name these battles of the Ottoman conquest of the Balkans.
swap.text: A crusade organized by the king of Hungary, and containing many Germans and French, met crushing defeat at the hands of Bayezid I, aka the Thunderbolt, at this site on the Danube in 1396.
swap.clue: Another city by this name was founded on the Ambracian Gulf after the Battle of Actium by Augustus, and Paul directed Titus to visit him there in his Epistle to Titus.

question.text: Ante Pavelic founded this terrorist movement, whose members became military enforcers when the Axis Powers established the Independent State of Croatia. Hundreds of thousands of Serbs were executed at their death camps, such as Jasenovac.
question.clue: Along with the Nazi party, the Bigelow Report outed the Roman Catholic church for hiding this organization's gold.

swap.text: Tuđman launched Operation Storm and obliterated the forces of Serbian Krajina after agreeing to lend this leader military aid via the Split Agreement. With Tuđman and Slobodon Milosevic, this first President of Bosnia and Herzegovina signed the 1995 Dayton Accords.
